text:
support: FYI multiple customers reporting 503s for hosted inference on redwood-7b-v1 around 12:03 UTC. Tickets #C1234, #C1235. Gateway shows upstream 500/503s and we see repeated runner restarts. attaching top lines of logs.

oncall: copying logs here, will start triage. any recent deploys?

devops: no deploys in the 1h window. autoscaler did a small scale-up at 11:52 but nothing else.

alex: log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:03:10Z] runner[pid=4123] ERROR: CUDA out of memory when allocating 128MB
[2026-03-17T12:03:10Z] runner[pid=4123] INFO: dumping kv-cache metrics
[2026-03-17T12:03:11Z] runner[pid=4123] SEGV at 0x0 (signal 11), terminating
[2026-03-17T12:03:11Z] kubelet: Killing container due to OOMKilled
```

maria: seeing the same pattern on nodes in us-west-2a. OOM then segfault then kube restarts. QPS spike correlates with ticket times.

sam: Is this the batchmap change we shipped last week? I remember a flag that changes batch packing heuristics.

devops: yes we toggled batchmap=true in the runtime config at 03/16 22:00 UTC (safe toggle). Could be related.

oncall: mitigation options: 1) route traffic for affected customers to a fallback model variant (redwood-7b-v1-small) or CPU pool 2) temporarily disable batchmap on the serving fleet 3) increase node memory on the gpu pool. Which is fastest?

eng-runtime: ping @eng-runtime — please advise on quick rollback plan for batchmap. If this is causing improper kv cache growth it could cause OOM.

eng-runtime: investigating. initial hypothesis: batchmap combined with prefix caching caused unexpected kv-cache retention when many short contexts hit hot prefixes -> memory blowup. We can roll flag back per-cluster.

infra-bot: Rolled out batchmap=true to cluster: hosted-us-west-2 (6 nodes) on 2026-03-16T22:01:03Z. Canary passed 30m.

sre-bot: Observed memory metric spike on hosted-us-west-2/gpu-pool-2 at 12:02 UTC: host_mem_used went from 60%->95% in 90s. Container OOMs increased +18 in 5m.

alex: Repro attempt locally: run load test with many short-context batched requests. After ~2000 requests memory climbs steadily, then OOM. We can reproduce with batchmap=on + kv_prefetch=on.

maria: Can we flip batchmap=false on the cluster and see if crashes stop?

eng-runtime: I'll prepare a targeted rollback for hosted-us-west-2. Quickest path: disable batchmap via runtime config and restart the runners gracefully (rolling restart). Will push change in 5m if approved.

oncall: Approve. Also enable fallback routing for impacted customers to cpu-backend for now to reduce customer impact. Support, please notify customers that we're triaging and have a temporary mitigation.

support: Notifying customers now: "We're seeing upstream worker restarts causing 503s. We've enabled fallbacks and are rolling back a recent batching optimization; we'll update in 30m." :phone:

devops: disabling batchmap on hosted-us-west-2 now (changing config key runtime.optimizations.batchmap=false) and issuing rolling restart of runner pods (maxUnavailable=1).

infra-bot: Config change applied to hosted-us-west-2 at 12:12:05Z. Rolling restart started.

sre-bot: After first 2 nodes restarted: container restarts per minute dropped from 14->2. 503 rate for redwood-7b-v1 decreased 78%.

alex: After rollback, load test no longer trips OOM locally with same traffic profile (batchmap off). Good sign.

eng-runtime: We'll keep cluster in rollback state for 24h while we dig into root cause. Likely causes: batchmap packing + kv-prefetch retention + specific sequence lengths causing exponential kv growth. Next steps: add additional kv limits, add kv cache accounting to runtime, and prepare a safe re-roll with tighter caps.

maria: Assigning follow-up: eng-runtime to own RCA and a patch before re-enabling. oncall to monitor memory and restart counts for 6h. support to follow up with customers in 2h.

support: Customer update posted: "We've mitigated the immediate impact by rolling back a batching optimization and enabling fallbacks. We're investigating root cause and will follow up in 2 hours with details."

oncall: Closing incident ticket for immediate outage; tracking task: INF-4721 (RCA + patch) assigned to eng-runtime.

eng-runtime: Will produce RCA and a reproduction script. Also will add a canary that runs short-context load profile before enabling batchmap cluster-wide.

support: Thanks team. Customers on the two impacted accounts acknowledged the update and are waiting for RCA.

sam: note for postmortem: ensure we have perf tests that exercise many short contexts + prefix reuse.

maria: logging follow-up: save core dumps and attach to INF-4721. I collected cores from three nodes and uploaded to S3 s3://redwood-incident-dumps/3355559999/

alex: marking repro steps in ticket: run local load harness with batchmap=true, kv_prefetch=true, 8 concurrent clients, context lengths mostly 8-32 tokens, seed data with repeated prefixes. Repro in ~2k requests.

support: I'll keep the customers updated on progress. If anything changes ping @support. :white_check_mark:

oncall: Monitoring continues. Will post any regression.

eng-runtime: ETA for RCA doc: 48h. Will include fix plan and safe re-roll checklist.

support: Thanks everyone, moving to post-incident tracking.
